mainTopic: An אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו, and how a מנחת העומר whose קמיצה was done שלא לשמה can go on the מזבח
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of רב's ruling that an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו is invalid. A ברייתא says such an אשם is still offered on the מזבח, and the מצורע just needs another one, so רב is refuted with a תיובתא. The גמרא then turns to ריש לקיש's ruling: a מנחת העומר whose קמיצה was done שלא לשמה is valid, but its leftovers stay forbidden until a second עומר is brought. The question is how its handful can go on the מזבח if the new grain is still forbidden to ישראל. רב אדא בר אהבה answers with the rule אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום, meaning something that becomes permitted that same day already counts as permitted. That answer survives a challenge from a ברייתא comparing birds and מנחות. It also survives רב ששת's challenge from the מצורע's oil, which רב פפא answers by saying the מצורע's order is special. But רב פפא's own challenge, about a חטאת slaughtered before the אשם, leaves the rule in trouble. So רב פפא gives a new reason: ריש לקיש holds that dawn itself permits the new grain. He begins to prove this from a joint statement of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Source showing a נזיר is not made fit by one specific offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its earlier distinction about the נזיר with a teaching: if he shaved after any one of his three offerings, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: If he shaved after any one of the three of them, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to support what it just said about the נזיר. It quotes a teaching that a נזיר who shaved after any one of his three offerings has fulfilled his duty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's reason is that an offering which comes to make someone fit must be brought לשמו. The נזיר's case is different. No single offering is the one that makes him fit, since shaving after any of the three works. So the נזיר's offerings do not challenge רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow to abstain from wine, haircuts, and contact with the dead
He shaved (the נזיר's shaving at the end of his term)
From the three of them (his חטאת, עולה, and שלמים)
He has fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: As the Master said:
If he shaved after one of the three of them, he has fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: The three are the נזיר's חטאת, עולה and שלמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer, given before this section, that the נזיר's offerings are different from the אשם מצורע.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that no specific offering of the נזיר is what makes him fit
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that shaving after any one of the three offerings is enough

steps.title: A ברייתא says the אשם מצורע slaughtered not for its sake is still offered
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו, or whose blood was not placed on the thumbs and toes, is still offered on the מזבח with נסכים. The מצורע just needs another אשם to make him fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: An אשם מצורע that was slaughtered not for its own sake, or whose blood was not put on the thumb and big toe, is still offered on the מזבח and needs נסכים. But the מצורע needs another אשם to make him fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says this אשם is still a valid offering, even though it did not make the מצורע fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said this אשם is invalid because it failed to make the מצורע fit. The ברייתא separates two things. The offering itself is valid and goes on the מזבח with נסכים. It just does not do the job of making the מצורע fit, so he needs a second one.

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt offering a recovered מצורע brings as part of his purification
Not for its own sake (slaughtered with the wrong intent)
The right thumb and right big toe, where the blood is placed
Libations (wine, flour and oil brought with certain offerings)
To make him fit (to eat קדשים)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say the offering is invalid. It says the offering is valid and still goes on the מזבח. Only its effect of making the מצורע fit is missing.

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: אָשָׁם מְצוֹרָע שֶׁנִּשְׁחַט שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: They raised an objection: a leper's guilt offering that was slaughtered not for its own sake,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִיתַּן מִדָּמוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהוֹנוֹת –
phrases.english: or none of its blood was placed on the thumb and big toe,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה עוֹלֶה לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, וְטָעוּן נְסָכִים,
phrases.english: this goes up on the altar, and it requires libations,
and he needs another guilt offering to make him fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the נזיר challenge is handled, the גמרא attacks רב directly from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats this exact case as a valid offering that goes on the מזבח. It only adds that another אשם is needed to make the מצורע fit.

steps.title: רב's view is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares the ברייתא a decisive refutation of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds no answer for רב and declares his view refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא means the ruling cannot stand against the ברייתא. The הלכה follows the ברייתא: such an אשם is valid, but it does not make the מצורע fit.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; the view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: An אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו is still a valid offering on the מזבח. The מצורע simply needs another אשם to become fit. רב's view that it is invalid was refuted.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from the ברייתא by rejecting רב's view.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's ruling is rejected; the אשם is valid but does not make the מצורע fit.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן לקיש on an עומר whose קמיצה was done not for its sake
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש rules that a מנחת העומר whose קמיצה was done שלא לשמה is valid. Its leftovers cannot be eaten until another עומר is brought to permit the new grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: A מנחת העומר from which the כהן took the handful not for its own sake is valid. But its leftovers may not be eaten until another מנחת העומר is brought and permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of the מנחת העומר and quotes רבי שמעון בן לקיש's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר is what permits the new grain (חדש) to be eaten. If its קמיצה was done שלא לשמה, the offering itself is still valid. But it has not done its job of permitting the new grain. So its own leftovers stay forbidden until a second עומר is brought.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley meal offering brought on the sixteenth of ניסן that permits the new grain
The כהן taking a handful from a meal offering to burn on the מזבח
Valid
Its leftovers (what remains after the handful, eaten by the כהנים)

steps.whyThisMatters: This follows the same pattern as the ברייתא about the אשם מצורע. The offering is valid, but its special effect does not happen, so another one is needed.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר שֶׁקְּמָצָהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ – כְּשֵׁירָה,
phrases.english: an omer meal offering from which he took the handful not for its own sake is valid,
but its remainder may not be eaten

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁתָּבִיא מִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר אַחֶרֶת וְתַתִּירֶנָּה.
phrases.english: until another omer meal offering is brought and permits it.
phrases.notes: The second עומר is the one that actually permits the new grain, including this first one's leftovers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with רב and the אשם מצורע, the גמרא returns to the earlier discussion of the מנחת העומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עומר whose קמיצה was done שלא לשמה is valid, but its leftovers stay forbidden until a second עומר is brought.

steps.title: How can a forbidden עומר be offered on the מזבח?
steps.stepSummary: If the leftovers are still forbidden as new grain, the עומר itself should not be allowed on the מזבח. The פסוק ממשקה ישראל teaches that only what is permitted to ישראל may be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If its leftovers may not be eaten until another עומר is brought, how could it be offered at all? The פסוק says 'from the well-watered pastures of Israel,' meaning only from what is permitted to ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן לקיש's ruling. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן לקיש admits the new grain is still forbidden, since the leftovers cannot be eaten. But there is a rule from the פסוק that the מזבח only receives what ישראל may eat. So how could the handful from this still-forbidden grain be burned on the מזבח?

keyTerms.meaning: To be offered (on the מזבח)
From the well-watered pastures of Israel (יחזקאל 45:15)
Only from what is permitted for ישראל to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the leftovers with the handful. The leftovers are eaten by the כהנים, and the handful is burned on the מזבח. The question is about the handful: how can it go on the מזבח if this grain is still forbidden?

phrases.english: Since its remainder may not be eaten
until another omer meal offering is brought,
how can it be offered at all?
"From the well-watered pastures of Israel" – from what is permitted to Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי שמעון בן לקיש's ruling using his own statement that the leftovers are still forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן לקיש's ruling that the עומר is valid and is offered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The leftovers are still forbidden as new grain, and the מזבח only receives what is permitted to ישראל. So the handful from this עומר should not be allowed on the מזבח.

steps.title: Permitted later the same day is not 'too early'
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that ריש לקיש holds אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום. Since the new grain becomes permitted that same day, the עומר already counts as fit for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: ריש לקיש holds that something which will become ready on that same day is not considered 'not yet ready.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5: how can the עומר go on the מזבח if new grain is still forbidden to ישראל? רב אדא בר אהבה says it is fine, because the new grain will become permitted later that same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 5 assumed that anything still forbidden to ישראל cannot go on the מזבח. רב אדא בר אהבה answers that a lack which will be fixed on the same day does not count as a lack. So the עומר's grain is treated as already permitted, even though the leftovers must wait for a valid עומר.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; this is his legal view
Missing time; something whose time to be used or offered has not yet come
On that same day

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום, is a general rule. It lets ריש לקיש's ruling stand, but it now has to survive the challenge that follows.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Reish Lakish holds
that something is not considered 'lacking time' if it becomes ready that same day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אדא בר אהבה קסבר ריש לקיש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5, which used the פסוק ממשקה ישראל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a general principle that removes the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Grain that is still forbidden to ישראל cannot go on the מזבח, so the עומר should be unfit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the new grain becomes permitted that same day, it is not considered forbidden, and the עומר may go on the מזבח.

steps.title: A ברייתא contrasting birds and מנחות
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בריה דרב יצחק objects by quoting a ברייתא that lists differences between bird offerings and מנחות. The first difference: two people may jointly donate a bird, but a מנחה must come from one person, because the פסוק says נפש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא son of רב יצחק raised an objection: Some rules apply to birds and not to מנחות, and some apply to מנחות and not to birds. What applies to birds? Birds can be donated by two people together, but for מנחות the פסוק says 'a soul,' meaning one person.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא begins to challenge רב אדא בר אהבה's answer by quoting a ברייתא. This first part sets up the list and gives its first item; the part that matters for the objection comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares two kinds of offerings that seem similar, birds and מנחות, and lists where they differ. The first difference is about who may donate. Two partners may give a bird, but the word נפש teaches that a מנחה comes from a single person. This item is background; it is not yet the point of the attack.

keyTerms.meaning: Birds; here, bird offerings
Meal offerings, made of flour
A voluntary gift offering brought jointly by two people
Literally 'a soul'; in the פסוק about מנחה it means one individual

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַב אַדָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Adda, son of Rav Yitzchak, raised an objection:
There is something with birds that does not apply to meal offerings,
and there is something with meal offerings that does not apply to birds.
What there is with birds:
birds may come as a gift offering from two people together,
but with meal offerings, 'a soul' is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתיב רב אדא בריה דרב יצחק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to the answer of רב אדא בר אהבה in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's explanation of ריש לקיש (אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Builds a list from a ברייתא of differences between birds and מנחות. The attack itself rests on a later item in the list.

steps.title: Birds can turn forbidden into permitted, מנחות cannot
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. People who still need atonement (זב, זבה, יולדת, מצורע) bring birds, and birds have a case where something forbidden becomes permitted through holiness. The ברייתא says this is not so with מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, those who still need an atonement offering, a זב, a זבה, a woman after childbirth, and a מצורע, bring birds. And with birds, something normally forbidden was permitted in holiness, which is not so with מנחות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא. Its last line, that מנחות never have something forbidden becoming permitted in holiness, is the line the objection will be built on; the גמרא will spell out the challenge next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two more differences. First, people who still need atonement bring birds, not מנחות. Second, with birds, killing by pinching (מליקה) would normally make a bird forbidden to eat, but for a holy bird it is the proper way to offer it. The ברייתא says מנחות have no such case, and that claim is what will press against the idea that the עומר's grain can go on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: People still missing their atonement offering before they become fully pure
A woman who gave birth
A person with צרעת
Permitted out of their general prohibition; something normally forbidden that becomes allowed

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא itself is not the question. The גמרא quotes it in full now, but it will explain right after this how its final line challenges רב אדא בר אהבה.

phrases.english: And those who still lack atonement:
a zav, a zava, a woman after childbirth, and a metzora.
And they were permitted out of their general prohibition when holy,
phrases.notes: Pinching a regular bird's neck makes it forbidden to eat, but for a holy bird that same pinching is the proper way to offer it.

phrases.english: which is not so with meal offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: ומחוסרי כפרה זב וזבה יולדת ומצורע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the ברייתא quoted in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's claim that the עומר's grain counts as permitted for the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says מנחות never have something forbidden becoming permitted in holiness. This sets up a challenge to how the עומר's grain is treated, and the גמרא will spell it out next.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends: laws found only in meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list. מנחות need a כלי, תנופה and הגשה, and they can come from the ציבור as well as from an individual. None of this is true of birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are laws only for meal offerings: they need a vessel, waving and bringing near, and they can be brought by the community as well as by an individual. This is not so with birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of the ברייתא that רב אדא בריה דרב יצחק started. This step sets up his actual objection, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the opposite direction: laws that apply to מנחות but not to birds. This finishes the full comparison. The real attack, though, is built on the earlier line in step 8 that birds can be permitted through holiness and מנחות cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: A holy service vessel. A מנחה must be placed in one.
Waving the offering
Bringing the מנחה near to the corner of the מזבח
The community as a whole, as opposed to an individual

phrases.english: And there is [a law] with meal offerings
that meal offerings require a vessel,
and waving and bringing near,
and they exist for the community just as for an individual,
which is not so with birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in steps 7 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling from step 4, together with the defense in step 6
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This only completes the source. The attack itself is spelled out in the next step.

steps.title: If ריש לקיש is right, meal offerings would have such a case too
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בריה דרב יצחק makes his point. According to ריש לקיש, the מנחת העומר whose קמיצה was done שלא לשמה would be a מנחה permitted out of its prohibition through holiness. The ברייתא said no such case exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so, you can find this with meal offerings too: they were permitted out of their general prohibition through holiness. What case is that? The עומר meal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punch line of the challenge. The ברייתא said only birds have a case of 'forbidden made permitted through holiness,' but ריש לקיש's ruling seems to create one for מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under ריש לקיש, the new grain is still forbidden to ordinary people, because another עומר must be brought. Yet the קמיצה of this עומר goes on the מזבח. That looks exactly like 'forbidden, yet permitted through holiness,' which contradicts the ברייתא's claim that this is not so with מנחות.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted out of their general prohibition: something normally forbidden that became allowed
Holiness, meaning the setting of an offering on the מזבח
The barley offering brought on 16 ניסן, which permits the new grain

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if ריש לקיש is right that this עומר is valid.

phrases.english: with meal offerings too you would find it,
that they were permitted out of their general prohibition in holiness,
And what is it?
The omer meal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא, בִּמְנָחוֹת נָמֵי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא just finished to ריש לקיש's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that the עומר whose קמיצה was done שלא לשמה is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling would create a case of a מנחה permitted through holiness, and the ברייתא says there is no such case.

steps.title: Same-day permission means it was never really forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that because of אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום, the עומר is not a real prohibition that got permitted. It counts as fit from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is no 'lacking time' on that same day, it is not a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש using the same idea from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new grain will become permitted later that same day. So the עומר is treated as already permitted, and it is not 'forbidden.' Since there was never a real prohibition, this is not a case of 'forbidden made permitted,' and the ברייתא is not contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: Something whose time has not yet come
On that same day

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the new grain is permitted right now to everyone. It means that, for judging whether the עומר is fit for the מזבח, a permission coming later that day already counts.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום answers both challenges: the one from ממשקה ישראל and this one from the ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאֵין מְחוּסַּר זְמַן לְבוֹ בַּיּוֹם,
phrases.english: Since there is no 'lacking time' for that same day,
it is not a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאֵין מְחוּסַּר זְמַן לְבוֹ בַּיּוֹם
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: it was never a prohibition in the first place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עומר is forbidden and is then permitted through holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the permission comes that same day, the עומר was never truly forbidden.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes the order of the leper's oil placements
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא about purifying a מצורע. If the כהן put the oil before the blood, or put oil on the thumb and toe before the seven sprinklings, he must refill the oil and do it again in the right order.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objects: If the כהן placed the oil before placing the blood, he refills the oil and places oil again after the blood. If he did the thumb-and-toe placement before the seven sprinklings, he refills the oil and does the thumb-and-toe placement again after the seven.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת opens a new challenge by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the source, and the גמרא will explain the attack next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, oil placed too early does not count, even though the right time for it comes on that same day. So this seems to go against the idea of אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום, which ריש לקיש's defense depends on.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, who brings offerings and goes through a purification process
Placing the blood of the אשם on the מצורע's right thumb and big toe
Placing oil on the מצורע's right thumb and big toe
Thumb and big toe
The seven sprinklings of oil before ה'

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raises an objection:
If he placed the oil before placing the blood,
phrases.notes: The order is in ויקרא 14:14–17: first the blood, then the oil.

phrases.english: he fills it with oil
phrases.notes: He tops up the לוג of oil so that a full measure is used again.

phrases.aramaic: וְיַחֲזוֹר וְיִתֵּן שֶׁמֶן אַחַר מַתַּן דָּם,
phrases.english: and again places oil after placing the blood;
[if he did] the thumb-and-toe placement before the seven sprinklings,
he fills it with oil

phrases.aramaic: וְיַחֲזוֹר וְיִתֵּן מַתַּן בְּהוֹנוֹת אַחַר מַתַּן שֶׁבַע.
phrases.english: and again does the thumb-and-toe placement after the seven sprinklings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the defense in step 11, a new challenge begins from a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום used to defend ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An oil placement done before its proper time on that same day still does not count and must be redone. This suggests that early is early, even on the same day.

steps.title: Why redo the oil if it was put on the same day?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת finishes his challenge: if something done early on the same day is not 'lacking time', the out-of-order oil should count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that something done early on the same day is not considered 'lacking time', why should the כהן go back and put the oil on again? What he did, he did!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains why the ברייתא about the מצורע's oil is a problem. If 'same day' means it is not too early, the oil that was put on out of order should already be valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil was going to be put on the thumb and toe that same day anyway. If the rule אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום is true, doing it a little early should not matter. Yet the ברייתא says he must refill the oil and do it again, which suggests that early, even on the same day, is a real problem.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Lacking time': something done before its proper time, which makes it invalid
On that same day
He must go back and put it on again
What he did, he did. The act should already count

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אֵין מְחוּסַּר זְמַן לְבוֹ בַּיּוֹם,
phrases.english: And if you say there is no 'lacking time' on that same day,
phrases.notes: This is the idea the גמרא used in Step 11 to explain the עומר.

phrases.english: why should he go back and put it on again?
What he did, he did!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אֵין מְחוּסַּר זְמַן לְבוֹ בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge that began with the ברייתא quoted in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום used in Step 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If same-day early acts are fine, the out-of-order oil should not need to be redone, but the ברייתא says it must be redone.

steps.title: The laws of a מצורע are different
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the מצורע's purification must follow the exact order, because the Torah says 'תהיה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The laws of a מצורע are different, because the Torah uses the word 'being' about them. The verse says: 'This shall be the law of the מצורע.' 'Shall be' means it must stay exactly as it is written.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends the 'same day' idea by saying the מצורע is a special case. The Torah demands that his purification be done in its exact order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil had to be redone not because it was 'too early', but because the מצורע has a special rule that the order itself is required. The word תהיה teaches that every step must be done exactly as written. So the ברייתא in Step 12 does not disprove the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. Used to set a case apart from the general rule
'Being': the Torah's use of a form of the word 'to be' (תִּהְיֶה)
The law, or procedure, of purifying a מצורע
It must be as it is. The exact order is required

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שָׁאנֵי הִלְכוֹת מְצוֹרָע,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The laws of a leper are different,
since 'being' is written about them,
as the verse says:
'This shall be the law of the leper',
'shall be': it shall be as it is.
phrases.notes: In other words, keep it exactly as written, in the same order.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שָׁאנֵי הִלְכוֹת מְצוֹרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge from Steps 12-13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the challenge to a special case (the מצורע has its own rule)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The redoing of the oil shows that same-day early acts count as 'lacking time'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oil is redone only because a מצורע's purification must follow its exact order, learned from תהיה.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges from a חטאת slaughtered before the אשם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if a מצורע's חטאת was slaughtered before his אשם, we do not keep its blood stirred and wait. It is left to spoil and burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא raised an objection: If the כהן slaughtered the מצורע's חטאת before his אשם, another person should not stir its blood to keep it ready. Instead, it is left until its form spoils, and then it goes out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא quotes a ברייתא that seems to go against the 'same day' rule. The חטאת is thrown away instead of being used later that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם is supposed to come before the חטאת. If 'same day' is not too early, why not keep the חטאת's blood from clotting, bring the אשם, and then finish the חטאת? The ברייתא instead treats the early חטאת as ruined.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering
Guilt offering. For a מצורע it must come before the חטאת
Stirring its blood so it does not clot
Its form spoils. It is left overnight until it becomes invalid
The place where invalid offerings are burned

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַב פָּפָּא: הִקְדִּים חַטָּאתוֹ לַאֲשָׁמוֹ –
phrases.english: Rav Pappa raised an objection: If he put his sin offering before his guilt offering,
another should not be stirring its blood,
phrases.notes: Stirring keeps the blood liquid so it could still be used after the אשם.

phrases.english: rather, its form should spoil
and it goes out to the place of burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the rule, רב פפא himself brings a new challenge against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If same-day early acts are fine, the early חטאת could be kept and used after the אשם. Throwing it away suggests it counts as 'lacking time'.

steps.title: How can רב פפא challenge from a מצורע case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: רב פפא himself said the מצורע is different, so a מצורע case should not bother him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does רב פפא raise this objection? Wasn't it רב פפא himself who said that the laws of a מצורע are different, because 'being' is written about them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב פפא's challenge. His own answer from Step 14 should already explain why the order matters for a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 14 רב פפא said a מצורע's purification must follow its exact order. The case in Step 15 is also about a מצורע, so the same answer should cover it. The objection looks like it contradicts his own words.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
But isn't it so that...? Used to point out a contradiction
The laws of purifying a מצורע

phrases.english: Why is Rav Pappa raising an objection?
But isn't it Rav Pappa who said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאנֵי הִלְכוֹת מְצוֹרָע, דִּכְתִיבָא בְּהוּ הֲוָיָיה!
phrases.english: The laws of a leper are different, since 'being' is written about them!
phrases.notes: These are his own words from Step 14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the objection in Step 15 makes sense, given Step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own rule that a מצורע's order is required already explains the ברייתא, so his objection seems to have no force.

steps.title: Slaughtering is not a Temple service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב פפא's real difficulty. The 'exact order' rule covers only a true עבודה, and שחיטה is not one. So the early חטאת should be kept and used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what was difficult for רב פפא: Say that the rule applies only to a Temple service, and slaughtering is not a Temple service. So if early on the same day is not 'lacking time', another person should stir its blood, the אשם should be brought, and then the חטאת should be brought!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב פפא was really asking. His challenge still stands even with the מצורע rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of תהיה demands the correct order only for real services (עבודה). שחיטה does not count as a service. So slaughtering the חטאת early is not ruined by the order rule, and with אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום its blood could be kept and offered after the אשם. Since the ברייתא says to burn it instead, the 'same day' rule is challenged again.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what was difficult for him
These words apply only to... (limits a rule)
A true Temple service
Slaughtering is not counted as a Temple service

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not taking back his rule that a מצורע is different. He is saying that rule covers only real services (עבודה), so it does not explain the early שחיטה.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'exact order' rule of a מצורע (תהיה) is limited to עבודה. Since שחיטה is not an עבודה, the early חטאת is still a real challenge to אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַב פָּפָּא הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rather, this is what was difficult for Rav Pappa:
Say that this applies only to a service,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule that a מצורע's order must be exact.

phrases.english: and slaughtering is not a service,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אֵין מְחוּסַּר זְמַן לְבוֹ בַּיּוֹם –
phrases.english: and if there is no 'lacking time' on that same day,
let another stir its blood,
and let him bring the guilt offering,
and afterward bring the sin offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַב פָּפָּא הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by restating רב פפא's objection in a stronger way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the objection (narrowing the scope of the מצורע rule)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's objection contradicts his own rule that a מצורע's order must be exact.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exact-order rule applies only to an עבודה, and שחיטה is not an עבודה. So the objection against אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום stands.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without the order rule covering שחיטה, the same-day rule would let the חטאת be kept and offered after the אשם. The ברייתא's ruling to burn it contradicts this.

steps.title: רב פפא gives a new reason for ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא drops the earlier approach and explains that ריש לקיש's ruling is based on his view that dawn of the עומר day already permits the new grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: this is the reason of ריש לקיש. He holds that when the eastern sky lights up, that itself permits the new grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier explanation of ריש לקיש did not hold up, so רב פפא offers a completely new reason for his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the old reason has been dropped. The new idea is that, for ריש לקיש, the new grain becomes permitted at dawn, not by the עומר offering. This answers the question in step 5: by the time the קמיצה is offered, the grain is already permitted to ישראל, so ממשקה ישראל is satisfied.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the previous approach is dropped and a new one is coming.
This is the reason
The eastern sky lit up, meaning dawn has come
Permits. Here it means dawn makes the new grain allowed to eat.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב פפא is saying the עומר is pointless. He is only saying that, for ריש לקיש, the עומר is not the thing that permits the new grain. Dawn does that.
steps.whyThisMatters: It moves the explanation away from the order and timing of the offering itself, which caused the trouble in Steps 15-17. Instead it explains the ruling by asking what actually permits the new grain.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
This is the reason of Reish Lakish:
phrases.notes: This is about his ruling that a קמיצה of the עומר done not for its own sake is still valid.

phrases.english: that he holds the lighting up of the east permits.
phrases.notes: Once dawn breaks on the day of the עומר, the new grain is already allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 15-17 left the principle אין מחוסר זמן לבו ביום under attack. So רב פפא drops רב אדא בר אהבה's explanation from step 6 and gives ריש לקיש's ruling a new foundation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New underlying reason (replacing the rejected one)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's ruling was based on the idea that something done early on the same day does not count as lacking time.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש's ruling is based on his view that dawn, not the עומר, permits the new grain.

steps.title: Source showing ריש לקיש holds that dawn permits
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא supports his claim with a known statement of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, who both say that even when the בית המקדש stands, something holds. The statement finishes in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say: even at a time when the בית המקדש is standing...
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא starts quoting a statement to prove that ריש לקיש really holds that dawn permits the new grain. The quote is not finished here. The גמרא is setting up the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on the words 'even when the בית המקדש is standing.' You would expect the עומר offering to be what permits the new grain at a time when it can actually be brought. Saying 'even then' prepares a strong claim that dawn alone permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: The two of them, both
At a time when
The בית המקדש is standing

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish
both say:
Even at a time when the Temple is standing,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in Step 18 that ריש לקיש holds dawn permits the new grain.
steps.raayaObject: That ריש לקיש holds 'הֵאִיר מִזְרָח מַתִּיר'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A known joint statement of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about the time when the בית המקדש is standing. It continues in the next lines.
